note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), round 1. Written on 18 Oct after the device move, because no record for this task was recovered from the 15-17 Oct round. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict:
The gates reproduce exactly, but one compliance problem must be fixed. Re-running ./gb tier-f gates leaves gates.json byte-identical to the stored copy: solvability 10/10, 471 tokens, 5/5 variants pass V5, the start fails at V5 in f2p only, and 17/17 mutants reach V4 and are killed. build.py regenerates task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all five variants byte-identically in scratch. The schema validates, and the canary appears only in task.json. Licence, source (composed_chain, no file to hash, like every composed sibling), cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (none: an original composed item) and id/dir/split are consistent. The split rule holds: signature_split(reference) is test. All four sources share one block id, so the signature does not depend on connection order, and with no inert or rare blocks there is no signature shopping. Disjointness from reports/reference/training_task_specs.json holds: no training spec covers a decimator or anti-aliasing, and t10, t17 and t20 are receiver or resampler tasks. Tolerances follow the stated spec. The closest first-set item, gbf-test-13 (a build-family, single-stage anti-aliasing demo, also in test), shares the theme but not the family, structure or numbers, so it is not a near-duplicate. Problems:
(1) The mutation gate's 100 % kill rate depends on leaving out the survivors the author documented. Two single-parameter test-signal mutants survive and would drop the kill rate to 17/19 = 89.5 %, below the 90 % gate, and the 16 Oct oracle policy is not met.
(2) Set-level: equivalent structures, including the author's own v5, hash to train.
(3) Set-level: composed L2 is a plan deviation, already recorded.

findings.claim: The mutation gate passes (17/17 killed) only because the mutation set leaves out the survivors the author documented. The two simplest spec-breaking mutants of the stated 'keep the test signal' requirement change one parameter each, reach V5 and pass it. With them in the set, the kill rate is 17/19 = 0.895, below the 0.90 gate. spec_properties also omits the requirement. Both break the 16 Oct oracle policy: every requirement the instruction states must be checked.
findings.evidence: Re-running ./gb tier-f gates leaves gates.json byte-identical (mutation: valid 17, kill_rate 1.0). ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-20/muts/m_tone4700_amp0.grc and m_tone23750_amp0.grc (edit.set_param on the reference) reach V5 and pass with P3 0.262393, RMS 0.412535, peak 600 and P4 1.0, identical to the reference. gates.MIN_KILL = 0.90. MUTATIONS includes test-signal edits only where V5 happens to see them (tone_2900 amp 0.15, tone_600 freq x1.25). The build.py docstring says such answers are 'visible in the structural partial-credit score', but partial credit is not V5. Under the graph checks proposed in item-quality IQ1 (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-20/task_gc.json), both mutants are killed by the 'tone 4700/0.4' or 'tone 23750/0.6' check.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the IQ1 graph checks and spec property P5. Add the two amp-0 mutants, and optionally one that deletes an unwanted source, with breaks = P5. Remove authoring_notes.known_limitation and the matching docstring paragraph. Rebuild and re-run ./gb tier-f gates.

findings.claim: The split rule holds as written: signature(reference) is test, and the signature does not depend on connection order because all four sources share one block id. There are no inert or rare blocks, so this is not signature shopping. But equivalent structures, including the author's own variant v5, hash to train. A training-side composer that obeys signature_split may therefore generate a structural twin of this decimator test bench: a multi-tone Add followed by two decimating FIR stages.
findings.suggested_fix: Set-level decision for fix_plan: make the signature equivalence-aware (treat low_pass_filter, fir_filter_xxx and fft_filter_xxx as one class and drop inert blocks such as Throttle), and require that no equivalent form hashes to train. Otherwise, record in disjointness that training-side generators must not emit multi-tone Add -> two-stage decimating FIR chains.

findings.claim: A composed (hand-written) L2 item lies outside the sources the plans declare. Eval plan §4.3 allows only 'simple hand-written L1 chains', and the approved plan takes L2 items from converted examples. The same deviation is already recorded for gbf-test-13 (F3), which names gbf-test-20. It is a plan deviation, not an authoring error.

The ~80 example flowgraphs that ship with GNU Radio, permissively licensed community flowgraphs, and simple hand-written L1 chains.' reports/tier_f_reviews/round1/gbf-test-13.json, compliance F3, lists gbf-test-20.
findings.suggested_fix: Team decision: amend the source list in the plans, or note the deviation in review.notes and on the team sheet.

item-quality.verdict: A well-made filter-design item with one high-severity hole that must be fixed before acceptance. What works: the instruction is self-contained and solvable from the start graph. Two cutoffs have to move: stage 1 must pass 2.9 kHz and reject 23.75 kHz before it folds to 250 Hz, and stage 2 must pass 2.9 kHz and reject 4.7 kHz before it folds to 3.3 kHz. Every number the signal checks use is stated (96/24/8 kHz; the tones; 1 %, 5 %, 40 dB = 99.99 % between 550 Hz and 2.95 kHz; skip 2000), and the checks implement exactly the stated operationalisation. The amplitude ratio 0.6 within 5 % maps to a power share in [0.24522, 0.28413]. All tones and aliases are bin-centred at 8000 samples, and there is no DC, so the 18 Oct band_fraction fix changes nothing. The instruction leaks neither the solution nor the fault, and L2 / parameter-tune is correct (8 functional blocks, two rate changes, filtering). Valid alternatives pass V5: decimation 3x4, three stages 2x2x3, one rational resampler 1:12, an fft_filter stage 2, Blackman windows, textbook margins, 4 kHz/2 kHz + 3.5 kHz, and the 15 Oct scratch alternatives (single stage, Throttle, band-pass stage 2, absolute file path). Wrong designs fail for the stated reason; for example, a Hann stage 1 with its passband edge at 3 kHz is -0.64 dB at 2.9 kHz and fails the stated 5 % ratio. The hole is that 'Keep the test signal, the 96 kHz input rate ... unchanged' is stated but never checked. Answers that edit or delete the test tones therefore pass V5, including answers that skip the task's whole alias-rejection design. A minor point: the oracle needs 10000 output samples, but the instruction never says the flowgraph must keep running.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'Keep the test signal, the 96 kHz input rate and the float output to logger_8k.dat unchanged'. But V5 only sees the 8 kHz decimator output, and task.json has no graph_checks. So answers that edit or remove the test tones, or change the input rate, pass V1-V5. Some of them skip the point of the task, the alias-rejection design: once the 4.7 kHz and 23.75 kHz tones are silenced, filter settings that the item's own mutation set treats as wrong get full credit. build.py records this as a 'known limitation' because a second tap is impossible. Since 16 Oct, structural graph checks can close it.
findings.evidence: Ladder against the task's own task.json; every file below reaches V5 and passes (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-20/alts/). x_boost_tone_stage2_only changes only the stage-2 cutoff (1500 -> 3600) and raises tone_2900 amp from 0.3 to 0.906 to make up for stage 1's -9.6 dB at 2.9 kHz: P3 share 0.268, RMS 0.408, peak 600, P4 1.0. x_silence_unwanted_bad_filters sets tone_4700 and tone_23750 amp to 0, with stage-1 cutoff 30000 and stage-2 cutoff 5000, which are the reference's killed mutants 8 and 5: P3 0.265, RMS 0.413, P4 1.0. x_delete_unwanted_sources deletes both unwanted sources and gives the Add 2 inputs. x_park_4700_on_null_sink moves tone_4700 to a Null Sink, gives the Add 3 inputs and sets the stage-2 cutoff to 5000. x_input_rate_192k sets samp_rate 192000, stage-1 decim 8 and stage-2 samp_rate samp_rate/8. The single-parameter mutants muts/m_tone4700_amp0 and muts/m_tone23750_amp0 pass with values identical to the reference. The build.py docstring and task.json authoring_notes.known_limitation acknowledge the gap ('can pass V5 although the instruction says to keep the test signal'), and spec_properties has no property for it. implementation_plan.md, Oracle policy: 'Every requirement the instruction states must be checked.'

findings.claim: The oracle needs 10000 samples in logger_8k.dat (1.25 s at 8 kHz, or 120000 input samples). The instruction only says to ignore the first 2000 samples and never says the flowgraph must keep running. A correct retune whose run is limited to one second of input therefore fails V4 liveness. The 16 Oct policy asks the instruction to state when the oracle needs a long run. Severity is low because the start graph is unbounded and a retune has no reason to add a Head.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-20/alts/h_head_one_second.grc is the reference plus blocks_head(num_items 96000) after test_mix. Ladder: highest V3, first_failed V4, 'liveness: an observation point received too few items {logger: 8000}'. The same graph with num_items 960000 (h_head_ten_seconds) passes V5. task.json observation.run has n_items/min_items 10000. The instruction has no 'keeps producing samples until it is stopped' sentence; compare gbf-dev-01, gbf-test-02 and gbf-test-04. implementation_plan.md, Oracle policy: 'If the oracle needs a long run, the instruction states it.'
findings.suggested_fix: Append to INSTRUCTION: 'The flowgraph keeps producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' Optionally say that the checks use the 8000 samples after the first 2000, as gbf-dev-09 does. Rebuild and re-run the gates.
